title: fix(memory): measure view merge age from the pair last message
description: view.go:149-151 computes due = (tailTo - start)/2^(level+2) using a.Range() start, i.e. the pair FIRST message. The optchat spec says this is the buggy first version (the 2^2 changes nothing; the bug was first). It merges old pairs at ties and churns old lines. Reproduced with a temporary test at the spec T=10 case: golem merges 0-7 instead of the newest 8-9.
design: Use due = (tailTo - last)/2^level where last is the pair last message (second part Range end minus 1), equivalently (tailTo+1)/2^level - index. Drop the +2 weight. Keep the built-parent gate and oldest-of-equal tie-break.
acceptance_criteria: A unit test reproduces the spec T=10 view (parts 0+4, 4+4, 8+1, 9+1, tailTo=10) and asserts the newest pair (level0 8,9 into level1 index4) merges, not 0-7. Existing view and compactor tests pass under -race.
close_reason: Merge age now measured from the pair end (OptChat 3.2); bestMergeIndex extracted and regression test TestViewMergeOrderMeasuresFromPairEnd added; fractal tests pass under -race.

title: fix(memory): render live-head recent events into the main agent prompt
description: The main agent never sees the newest raw events. RenderCombined (pkg/memory/fractal/multi_store.go:179) renders only View.Render(), which excludes the newest LiveHeadCount (10) events (view.go:208). Only the subagent MemoryContext (pkg/golem/agent.go:488-508) and the TUI cockpit call LiveHeadEvents(). The main InstructionProvider (agent.go:527-580) calls RenderCombined only. Combined with IncludeContentsNone and a fresh session per turn (agent.go:526,763), the model sees the current message plus coarse summaries but not the immediately preceding exchange. A short turn (user+reply) leaves the next view empty.
design: Append view.LiveHeadEvents() formatted like the subagent path (agent.go:488) after RenderCombined in the InstructionProvider. Prefer a shared renderLiveHead helper used by both main and subagent paths. Ensure the current user message is not duplicated; consider raising DefaultLiveHeadCount and the 120-char per-event truncation.
acceptance_criteria: The InstructionProvider output contains the most recent raw events (id, kind, truncated text) in a dedicated block. A pkg/golem test seeds user/talk/tool events within the live-head window, renders the instruction via the provider, and asserts the recent user turn appears; after a second turn with fewer than LiveHeadCount intervening events the prior exchange is still visible verbatim. -race passes.
close_reason: Extracted buildInstruction/formatLiveHead and inject a bounded recent_live_head block into the main agent prompt (subagent path reuses it). In-flight user message is dropped to avoid duplication. Added TestBuildInstructionIncludesLiveHead and TestFormatLiveHeadBoundsAndKeepsNewest; pkg/golem tests pass under -race.

title: Fractal memory rapid-forgetting: restore short-term context and fix the view algorithm
description:
Audit found that Golem loses recent context (moves short-term into long-term far too fast) and mis-locates itself across sessions/repos. Four root causes confirmed by reading the code and reproducing the merge order against the real fitLocked:

1. The main agent prompt never renders the live head. RenderCombined (pkg/memory/fractal/multi_store.go:179) renders only View.Render(), which excludes the newest LiveHeadCount (10) events. Only the subagent path (pkg/golem/agent.go:488) and the TUI cockpit consume LiveHeadEvents(). With IncludeContentsNone and a fresh session per turn (agent.go:526,763), the model sees the current message plus coarse summaries, but not the immediately preceding exchange. Short turns leave the view empty.

2. The merge-age formula measures from the pair first message, the exact bug the optchat spec warns against. view.go:149-151 computes due = (tailTo - start)/2^(level+2). Reproduced against fitLocked at the spec T=10 case: it merges the oldest pair 0-7 instead of the newest 8-9.

3. Merges run on every event with no low-water mark. fitLocked merges until size <= 128000 and is called after every append (view.go:117-121,128). The spec batches from 128 KB down to 64 KB; golem pins the view at the ceiling and can cascade-coarsen recent lines on every tool/echo event.

4. Overlong summaries are silently truncated (compactor.go:80,146) instead of retried, and the claimed 512-byte ruler is actually 505 bytes (compactor.go:26).

Outcome: recent raw events are always in context; the view coarsens in the correct order and only in batches; summaries are not silently clipped; the view survives restart.
design: Fix order: (1) live-head injection (biggest user-visible win), (2) merge-age formula, (3) batching+low-water, (4) view persistence, (5) summary retry+ruler. Each fix ships with a regression test. Finish with an adversarial code review.
acceptance_criteria: All child issues closed; pkg/memory/fractal and pkg/golem tests pass with -race; a fresh short session retains the prior turn in context.
close_reason: All 12 children complete: 5 fixes + review + 5 review findings, all with tests; full go test -race ./... green. Committed as cde1833 and d057ce9.

title: fix(memory): batch view merges with a 64 KB low-water mark
description: fitLocked merges to the 128 KB ceiling after every appended event (view.go:117-121,128), so each new tool/echo event can trigger a cascade that coarsens recent lines. The spec batches: grow to 128 KB, then merge down to 64 KB once, and between batches the view only grows at its end.
design: Add LowWaterBytes (default 64000) to ViewConfig; keep ViewBudgetBytes as the high-water alias. fitLocked targets low-water and is only entered when size > high-water. Keep per-append Sync cheap.
acceptance_criteria: Merging runs only when size exceeds a high-water mark (default 128000) and merges down to a low-water mark (default 64000) in one batch. A test asserts a single append while under high-water performs no merge, and that after a batch the size is <= low-water. No old line churns between batches.
close_reason: View now batches: fitLocked is a no-op at/below the high-water mark and merges in one pass down to a configurable low-water mark (default high/2). Added TestViewBatchingRespectsHighAndLowWater; fractal tests pass under -race.

title: fix(memory): persist the view across restarts instead of rebuilding
description: NewView always calls Rebuild (view.go:76). The optchat spec lists rebuilding the view at restart as mistake #3: the rebuilt tiling can differ from the live one and re-coarsens detail, and it kills the prompt cache. There is no view persistence today (store has events, nodes, metadata buckets only).
design: Persist parts plus tailTo in a bbolt bucket keyed per store; validate on load against CountEvents and the configured LiveHeadCount. Update on Sync/batch merges, not on every event if that is expensive.
acceptance_criteria: The view tiling is saved after changes and loaded on OpenStore/NewView. A test creates a store+view, syncs, closes, reopens, and asserts the rendered view equals the pre-close render. Rebuild is a fallback only when no saved view exists or it is inconsistent with the event count.
close_reason: View tiling is now persisted to a bbolt view bucket and loaded on NewView; falls back to Rebuild only when absent/inconsistent. Added TestViewPersistsAcrossRestart; fractal tests pass under -race.

title: Swarm A: thread SubagentID back through InvokeResult so the orchestrator can address peers
description: InvokeResult carries Role, ModelUsed, Output, ToolCalls, Duration, Error but not SubagentID. The ID (subagent-<role>-<unixnano>) is generated inside Runner.Invoke and only whispered to the subagent via its system prompt, so the orchestrator can never actually address a running peer with send_message — the 'peer agents' story breaks at the ID round-trip. Add SubagentID to InvokeResult (and the subagent_done event), and surface it in the invoke_subagent tool result header so the orchestrator learns the ID. Part of Swarm lane A (wake it up).
close_reason: Added SubagentID to InvokeResult and Event; Runner.Invoke generates the id up front and sets it on every result + subagent_start/done events; invoke_subagent result header now reports 'id: <subagent-id>' so the orchestrator can address peers.

title: Swarm B: broadcast_message and send_message to unknown agents silently vanish (Subscribe never called)
description:
Live swarm testing shows messaging primitives are not wired for delivery:

1. NewToolset never calls Bus.Subscribe, so no agent ever subscribes to a channel. broadcast_message returns success but reaches nobody. (Subscribe in pkg/swarm/bus.go:167 has zero non-test call sites.)
2. Bus.Send returns nil even when the recipient has no mailbox: it creates the mailbox and delivers, but the message is only seen if the recipient calls check_inbox in the same run. A message to a finished/unknown agent disappears.
3. InvokeResult now carries SubagentID (Lane A), but a subagent finishes before the orchestrator can message it, so the id is only useful for messages sent DURING the subagent run.

Options to discuss: (a) have the orchestrator subscribe to channels and surface broadcasts via an unread-style nudge (like <swarm_inbox>); (b) route undeliverable mail to a dead-letter/DLQ the orchestrator is nudged about; (c) have subagents on the shared bus subscribe to 'orchestrator-directives' and drain at step boundaries; (d) make send to an unknown agent return an explicit warning. Part of Swarm lane B.
close_reason: Fixed by lane B delivery guarantees. (a) The orchestrator + every subagent now Register on the bus (NewToolsetWithSession), so broadcast_message fans out to all live agents' mailboxes -- no Subscribe needed -- and the <swarm_inbox> nudge surfaces unread broadcasts. (b) send_message to an unknown/offline agent is detected: Bus.Send returns DeliveryDeadLetter, parks the message in a bounded dead-letter queue, and the tool tells the sender 'could NOT be delivered ... registered agents are: [...].' (c) Subagents register for the lifetime of their run and unregister at the end; the orchestrator sees peer ids via the invoke_subagent header. See golem-c8y.

Found in the golem-sma.3 review.

If the tail window ends on a tool whose echo never arrived (e.g. a turn interrupted mid-tool, or the event cap splitting a pair), the replay renders a ghost RUNNING tool card in historical output. Force every replayed tool to a terminal state after building the entries. Found in the golem-sma.3 review.
acceptance_criteria: A tool event with no matching echo in the replay window renders as finished, not running; a test covers a trailing unpaired tool.
close_reason: eventsToEntries now forces every replayed tool to a terminal state, so an interrupted/pair-split tool cannot replay as RUNNING. Test: TestEventsToEntriesTrailingToolNotRunning.

title: fix(memory): catch up the persisted view instead of full rebuild on TailTo mismatch
description: loadStateLocked (pkg/memory/fractal/view.go) rejects the saved tiling whenever saved TailTo != total - LiveHeadCount, which is exactly the crash case: events appended after the last view save. It then falls back to a full Rebuild, re-coarsening detail and defeating the persistence goal. Fix: when saved TailTo < expected, load the saved tiling and append level-0 parts for [savedTail, expectedTail) then re-fit, instead of rebuilding from 0. Rebuild only when the saved tiling is geometrically invalid or saved TailTo > expected.
acceptance_criteria: A store with a saved view behind by N events loads and catches up to the current tail without a full Rebuild; a test covers it.
close_reason: loadStateLocked now loads a saved tiling whose TailTo lags the store and catches it up with level-0 parts + re-fit instead of a full rebuild; Rebuild only when the tiling is invalid or extends past the tail. Added TestViewCatchesUpPersistedTiling.

title: fix(memory): bound node size if the summarizer never converges
description: SummarizeBounded (pkg/memory/fractal/compactor.go) removed the previous truncateUTF8 hard cap. If the compactor model returns an over-length line on all maxSummaryCorrections attempts, the oversized node is stored as-is, and Render/calculateSizeBytes then carry an arbitrarily large line (prompt bloat). OptChat tolerates a few bytes over 512, not 100x. Fix: add a generous last-resort safety cap (e.g. 4x DefaultNodeTargetBytes) applied only after the retry loop is exhausted, and surface a signal (log or memory stat) when it triggers.
acceptance_criteria: A summarizer that always returns a huge line yields a stored node within the safety cap, and the cap event is visible (not silent).
close_reason: SummarizeBounded now caps at maxNodeBytes (4x target) after the correction loop and logs when it triggers, so a non-converging model cannot store an unbounded node. Added TestSummarizeBoundedCapsNonConverging.

title: test(review): make the view-persistence test actually prove loading
description: TestViewPersistsAcrossRestart (pkg/memory/fractal/view_test.go) asserts the rendered view is equal before and after reopen, but Rebuild is deterministic given the same nodes and config, so an identical tiling is expected even if load never ran. The test cannot fail if persistence regresses to a rebuild. Fix: before NewView, call store.SaveViewState with a valid-but-non-rebuild tiling (e.g. 16 level-1 parts over tail 32 where a rebuild would produce 32 level-0 parts) and assert NewView returns exactly that tiling. Found during the golem-sid.7 review.
acceptance_criteria: The test fails if NewView rebuilds instead of loading, and passes with load.
close_reason: Added TestViewLoadsPersistedTilingNotRebuild: injects a valid non-rebuild tiling (16 level-1 parts) and asserts NewView returns exactly it, so the test fails if persistence regresses to a rebuild.

title: fix(memory): retry over-length summaries instead of truncating and correct the 512-byte ruler
description: Summarizers silently truncate to 512 bytes (compactor.go:80,146) via truncateUTF8, dropping the tail of long summaries. The prompt claims the reference ruler is exactly 512 bytes; it measures 505 (compactor.go:26). The spec says to resend a Too long correction up to 5 times and keep the shortest line.
design: Enforce length with a retry wrapper around the Summarizer contract (or inside Compactor.BuildNode) that appends the Too long correction and re-calls. Fix the ruler constant to exactly 512 bytes.
acceptance_criteria: A too-long summary triggers a correction follow-up up to 5 times, keeping the shortest candidate; a fake summarizer test proves the retry path and that no stored node is silently clipped. A test asserts len(ScaleLine512Bytes) == 512. -race passes.
close_reason: Summarizers no longer truncate: added CorrectingSummarizer + SummarizeBounded which resends the Too long correction up to 5 times and keeps the shortest candidate; BuildNode uses it. Ruler now exactly 512 bytes. Added TestScaleLineIsExactly512Bytes and TestSummarizeBoundedCorrectsOverLength. Full go test -race ./... green.

title: Swarm A: surface unread swarm mail at turn start (inbox nudge)
description: Nothing drains or surfaces unread swarm mail when a turn begins. If a subagent sends a message mid-run it sits in the mailbox until the model happens to remember check_inbox. Inject a lightweight 'you have N unread swarm messages' notice into the turn context (like the memory view / live head), using Mailbox.UnreadCount(), without draining. Part of Swarm lane A (wake it up).
close_reason: Added Bus.UnreadCount(agentID); orchestrator InstructionProvider injects <swarm_inbox>N unread...</swarm_inbox> when mail is pending, without draining. Regression test TestSwarmBusUnreadCount.

title: Swarm B: make it an actual swarm (async delegation, enforced locks, lock events)
description: Lane B epic. Current swarm is mechanism-only and sequential. Sub-items: (1) async/parallel invoke_subagent fan-out + join instead of blocking functiontool; (2) enforce advisory locks inside hashline_patch/write_file/shell via ListLocks; (3) emit WSEventSwarmLock (currently defined but never emitted) and show locks in the cockpit; (4) per-subagent lifecycle on the bus; (5) populate Message.SessionID/Metadata; (6) consistent Broadcast semantics (channel handlers run inline/blocking while global listeners run async); (7) delivery guarantees — Send auto-creates mailboxes so messages to dead agents vanish silently, add ack/undeliverable handling. Do after lane A proves the value.
close_reason: Swarm lane B shipped. (1) Fan-out: ADK v2.5.0 platform.RunTasks already runs parallel tool calls concurrently with a completion barrier, so multiple invoke_subagent calls in one turn are a real fan-out+join. (2) Locks enforced at the edit layer: pkg/swarm/locks.go CheckToolLock refuses write_file/replace_regex/hashline_patch when another owner holds the resource; wired into the orchestrator BeforeToolCallback (pkg/golem/agent.go) and the subagent BeforeToolCallbacks (pkg/subagent/runner.go). ADK skips tool.Run and surfaces {error} so enforcement is real. (3) Lock events: Bus.OnLockChange -> WSEventSwarmLock in session_manager (both CreateSession paths, unsub on delete/close); UI Locks tab in SwarmTree.svelte + swarmLocks store. (4) Per-subagent lifecycle: NewToolsetWithSession registers the agent (+mailbox) and Runner defers Unregister; orchestrator registers as swarm.OrchestratorID. (5) Message.SessionID populated from toolset session. (6) Broadcast now fans to every registered agent's mailbox + safeCall channel handlers + async global listeners; returns delivery count. (7) Delivery guarantees: registered-agent registry, Send returns DeliveryStatus (delivered/dead_letter), bounded DLQ + dead-letter count, sender warned on undeliverable send. Tests: TestSwarmBusRegistryAndDeadLetter, TestSwarmBroadcastReachesUnsubscribedRegisteredAgents, TestSwarmLockEvents, TestCheckToolLock, TestToolsetRegistrationLifecycle. build/vet/race green, UI builds.

title: Harden memory-recursion guard and add regression test
description: Commit d2cae29 stopped recording zoom/date into memory to break a runaway recursion loop, but implemented it as two hardcoded tool-name comparisons (pkg/golem/agent.go ~582 BeforeToolCallbacks, ~625 AfterToolCallbacks). Fragile: renaming a read-only memory tool, or adding a new one, silently re-opens the loop. There is also no regression test guarding the behavior.
design: Introduce a single source of truth for 'do not persist this tool call' (e.g. a read-only/no-record attribute on the tool or a small helper) consulted by both callbacks instead of inline string comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: Both callbacks consult one shared predicate; a pkg/golem regression test asserts event count is unchanged after a zoom/date tool invocation and that the result still reaches the model.

title: fix(agent): avoid live-head duplication mid-turn
description: buildInstruction (pkg/golem/agent.go) drops the in-flight user event only when it is the newest event. Within a single turn that makes several model calls (tool use), later calls see the turn user message both in the runner conversation history and in the live head. Low impact, but wasteful and potentially confusing. Document the behavior or suppress the current turn user event for all calls in the turn.
acceptance_criteria: Either documented in code, or the turn user message does not appear in the live head on any model call within the turn.
close_reason: Agent now tracks the in-flight turn user event ID; the InstructionProvider excludes it from the live head on every model call of the turn (not just when newest). Added exclusion-filter assertions to the live-head tests.

acceptance_criteria: The sentence appears once; no other prompt text changes.
close_reason: Removed the duplicated subagent-shared-memory line from the system prompt.

title: polish(tui): startup replay nits (input-history bound, tool exit code, display width)

title: polish(tui): width-aware startup header and timestamp guard

Truncate the path to the viewport width and guard last-active when the timestamp is zero. Found in the golem-sma.3 review.
acceptance_criteria: The header fits the viewport width and a zero timestamp does not render an absurd age.
close_reason: Added clampLines (rune-safe, ellipsis) applied to the header at viewport width, and a zero-timestamp guard that omits the age. Tests: TestClampLines, TestFormatStartupHeaderZeroTimestamp.

title: chore(review): share the UTF-8 truncate helper and test low-water normalization

Nit 2: NewView normalization sets LowWaterBytes = ViewBudgetBytes/2, but tiny high-water values (ViewBudgetBytes=1) yield low=0 and this path is untested. Add a test and clamp low to at least 1 where sensible. Found during the golem-sid.7 review.
acceptance_criteria: One truncate helper; a test covers ViewConfig normalization including tiny high-water values.
close_reason: Exported fractal.TruncateUTF8 and removed the duplicate truncateSafe; added TestNewViewNormalizesWaterMarks and clamped low-water to >=1 for tiny high-water values.
